story: Mali's soldiers seized power in 2020 and again in 2021, promising to do what the French army and UN peacekeepers had not: defeat the jihadists. They expelled the French, brought in Russian Wagner mercenaries and formed an alliance with fellow juntas in Burkina Faso and Niger. In 2026, the jihadists brought the war to the capital's doorstep.

The al-Qaeda-linked JNIM began blockading fuel tankers from Senegal and Côte d'Ivoire in September 2025, cutting Bamako's electricity to six hours a day and closing schools. The blockade eased early this year. Then on 25 April, JNIM and the Tuareg-led Azawad Liberation Front launched coordinated offensives, and Defence Minister Sadio Camara, architect of the Russia partnership, was killed. On 28 April JNIM declared all roads into Bamako closed (Africanews). Junta leader Assimi Goïta disappeared from view for days before reappearing on television to insist the situation was "under control." By July, JNIM had pushed into southern Mali for the first time and was imposing hijab rules on public transport outside the capital. "If Mali collapses, everything collapses," a senior diplomat warned (Reuters via Gazette). Analysts think JNIM lacks the strength to take Bamako but could strangle the junta into negotiating, or into a coup from within.
briefing.power: A military junta. Goïta made himself president for a renewable five-year term in 2025 without an election, dissolved political parties and rules by decree with a transitional council. Mali left ECOWAS and formed the Alliance of Sahel States with Burkina Faso and Niger.
